To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) managers of firms in the same strategic group are more likely to engage in competitive actions against each other than against other firms; (2) the likelihood of competitive actions against firms in the same group is positively related to the level of competition within the group, but not to group heterogeneity; and (3) managers of firms within the same strategic group tend to reposition their firm towards the center of their group.

the competitive dynamics of firms are driven by the actions and reactions of managers, which are influenced by their perceptions of their firm and the industry.
